title: adversarial-review scope contract
description: The scope contract, written to disk before any subagent is dispatched. It pins what is being reviewed (a merge-base SHA, never a moving ref), who owns which file, and what nobody may report. Keyword use stays inside the conservative set the bundled stdlib validator walks: type, properties, required, items, enum, additionalProperties. Rules a conditional would express live in check-territories.py instead, matching the kit convention that a schema states shape and a script states semantics.

fixed_point.description: What the user supplied, verbatim, e.g. 'main' or a SHA. Kept for the report; never used to compute a diff.

merge_base_sha.description: git merge-base <fixed_point> HEAD, resolved once in preflight. Every diff in the run is computed from this SHA, so a branch moving under a multi-day round loop cannot silently change what is under review.

diff_cmd.description: The exact command every finder is handed. Captured once so no two territories can be reviewing different things.

dirty_tree_accepted.description: True only when the user overrode the clean-tree check. Verification evidence is meaningful only against the code the diff describes, so an override is recorded rather than assumed.

excluded.description: Generated trees and vendored paths held out of territory derivation.

out_of_scope.description: Settled decisions, deliberate renames, prose-only changes. Passed verbatim to every finder as do-not-report.

changed_files.description: Every path in the diff after exclusions. Each one must be owned by exactly one territory.

entries.description: Literal repo-relative paths, or directory prefixes ending in '/'. A glob here would own nothing; check-territories.py rejects one.

classes.description: The union of suspicion classes this territory's files triggered. A file that is both money and authz keeps both lenses.

derivation.description: One record per changed file naming the trigger rows it matched and the territory it landed in. This is what makes the same diff produce the same territories twice.

amendments.description: Scope changes made mid-run, always when a later round's fix diff touched a path no territory owned. An amendment is recorded and re-validated rather than assumed.

rounds.description: One record per round. head_sha anchors the next round's fix diff; without it, 'territories the fix touched' has no definition and every round would intersect everything.
